legend: In ancient Carthage, scholars created a secret numerical cipher to protect their most valuable trade secrets. This cipher, believed to be a function f$$$f$$$, that maps each natural number to a secret value, was known only to the High Council of Merchants. The cipher was lost when Rome destroyed Carthage in 146 BC.
For centuries, archaeologists have searched for the legendary "Stone of Accounts", the key to unlocking this ancient secret.

Recently, in the ruins of ancient Carthage near modern-day Tunis, you've discovered the fabled Stone of Accounts! It's a mysterious device with two input slots and one output display. Ancient Punic inscriptions explain how it works: "Place two numbered stones in the slots. If their numbers sum to a power of two, the stone reveals the sum of their hidden values. Otherwise, it reveals nothing."
Formally, The Stone accepts two positive integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$:
If n+m$$$n+m$$$ is a power of two, it outputs f(n)+f(m)$$$f(n)+f(m)$$$

Centuries ago, archaeologists discovered ancient Carthaginian scrolls containing encrypted trade secrets: S=[S1,…,Sn].$$$S=[S_1,\dots,S_n].$$$ For generations, scholars have tried to decipher them, but without the Stone of Accounts, all attempts failed.
Now, with the Stone finally discovered, you have a chance to succeed where others could not.
Your mission: Recover the true message M=[f(S1),…,f(Sn)].$$$M=[f(S_1),\dots,f(S_n)].$$$ But be careful! The Stone is ancient and fragile. You can use it at most 10,000 times before it breaks forever.
input: The first line contains one integer 1≤n≤100$$$1 \le n \le 100$$$, denoting the length of the encrypted message.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers 1≤S1,…,Sn≤1018$$$1 \le S_1,\dots,S_n \le 10^{18}$$$, denoting the encrypted message.
Your program will interact via standard input/output with the black box.
Starting from i=1$$$i=1$$$, two modes of operations are supported:

Query the Stone, ? n m: You give two positive integers 1≤n,m<264$$$1 \le n,m  \lt  2^{64}$$$ to the Stone. The Stone responds with R s where:   s=f(n)+f(m)$$$s=f(n)+f(m)$$$ if n+m$$$n+m$$$ is power of two
Declare a Decrypted Value, ! d: This means you've determined that d=f(Si)$$$d=f(S_i)$$$. After this command:   You receive N.
You move to the next encrypted number: i←i+1$$$i\leftarrow i+1$$$
When all numbers are decrypted, your program can exit.
note: It is guaranteed that f$$$f$$$ exists and is unique.
It is guaranteed that: ∀n∈N,f(n)≤1018$$ \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \quad f(n) \le 10^{18} $$

legend.ai: 在古代迦太基，学者们创造了一种秘密数字密码，以保护他们最有价值的贸易机密。这种密码被认为是一个函数 f$$$f$$$，它将每个自然数映射为一个秘密值，只有商人最高议会知晓。公元前146年罗马摧毁迦太基时，这种密码也随之失传。
几个世纪以来，考古学家一直在寻找传说中的“账目之石”，这是解开这一古老秘密的关键。

形式化地说，账石接受两个正整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$：
如果 n+m$$$n+m$$$ 是 2 的幂，它就输出 f(n)+f(m)$$$f(n)+f(m)$$$
几个世纪前，考古学家发现了包含加密贸易秘密的古代迦太基卷轴：S=[S1,…,Sn].$$$S=[S_1,\dots,S_n].$$$ 几代学者一直尝试破译它们，但没有账石，所有尝试都失败了。
如今，随着账石终于被发现，你有机会完成前人未能做到的事情。
你的任务是：恢复真实消息 M=[f(S1),…,f(Sn)]。$$$M=[f(S_1),\dots,f(S_n)].$$$ 但请小心！这块石头古老而脆弱。在它永远损坏之前，你最多只能使用它 10,000 次。
